12.0.0.en: The tribe of Ephraim was accustomed to protest against the leaders of the people, as they had protested against Gideon before, and he answered them humbly and calmed their anger (ch. 8:1-3). The tribe of Ephraim is always marked by pride, which drives them to anger and objection, and now they not only object to Jephthah but gathered the men of war and went north and crossed the Jordan to fight Jephthah, and threatened to burn him and his house and all who were in it, and made the false claim that he had not asked them to join him in fighting the children of Ammon. The truth is that he had called them, but they were slack in answering his call. It appears that they were marked by stubbornness and protest, relying on their large numbers and strength, yet at the same time slack, speaking but not doing any positive work, rather stirring up problems. Their violence appears here in that they did not merely reproach him but threatened him with death.

12.0.1.en: It is clear that they were proud, for when Jephthah achieved the victory it was hard on them not to share in the glories of the victory, so the cause of their revolt was pride and not defending the people against the occupiers. It would have been more fitting for them to thank Jephthah for his bravery and to comfort him over his only daughter, but their pride made them hard of heart.

12.1.0.en: Jephthah reproached them that when he and his people, the men of Gilead, cried out to them, asking their support against the children of Ammon, they did not respond to their calls and left him and the men of Gilead to face the children of Ammon alone.

12.2.0.en: "I put my life in my hands": I faced the danger without fear, making light of death.

12.2.1.en: Jephthah told them that when it became clear to him that they were not ready to join him in his war against the children of Ammon, he was compelled to fight the battle with his people alone, and the Lord gave him victory over them. Therefore they have no right today to come out to fight him.

12.2.2.en: Be positive and do not stir up problems, and search in every matter for what you may learn for the benefit of yourself and all those around you, and do not create a problem to assert your personality. Be humble so that you may offer love to those around you and work for your good and the good of others.

12.3.0.en: "Ye Gileadites are fugitives of Ephraim": you are a band of fugitives from the tribe of Ephraim, because you are thieves and rabble and have no worth in society.

12.3.1.en: "Among the Ephraimites, and among the Manassites": the land of Gilead is adjoined by the land of Ephraim on the west and by the land of Manasseh on the east and on the north.

12.3.2.en: The Ephraimites who said this phrase meant to despise the Gileadites, for they were saying to them: You fled and settled in this region between the two tribes because you did not dare to settle in either of them, since you are outcasts and despised by both.

12.3.3.en: Jephthah gathered the warriors from Gilead and fought Ephraim and overcame them. Ephraim had been taunting the Gileadites that they were thieves, fugitives from their tribe.

12.4.0.en: "Fugitives of Ephraim": the Ephraimites, because of their feeling of defeat.

12.4.1.en: "The passages of Jordan": the shallow gatherings of water adjoining the river Jordan.

12.4.2.en: Shibboleth: a word meaning an ear of grain.

12.4.3.en: The men of Gilead seized the fords of the river Jordan so that the Ephraimites could not escape by them, and so that Jephthah's men could recognize the fugitives from the soldiers of Ephraim, they would arrest anyone who passed through these fords and ask him to say the word "Shibboleth." The men of Ephraim used to pronounce the letter shin as "sin." Since the fugitives were in fear and not expecting the question, they would say "Sibboleth," and the Gileadites would know that they were men of Ephraim and kill them, and in this way they killed 42,000 Ephraimite men, which is considered most of the army of Ephraim. Here the lack of wisdom in Jephthah appears, for he resisted the pride of Ephraim with his own pride, and so the people of God lost a great number of its sons; whereas Gideon is distinguished here from Jephthah by humility and wisdom.

12.5.0.en: The length of Jephthah's judging his people was short, six years, but full of the work of salvation and striving for his people, and he was buried in one of the cities of the region of Gilead.

12.6.0.en: Bethlehem: it is either the Bethlehem which is in the tribe of Zebulun and lies west of Nazareth at a distance of 9 km, or the one in the tribe of Judah, which lies south of Jerusalem at a distance of 9 km, and which is where Christ was born.

12.6.1.en: After the death of Jephthah, the next judge was Ibzan of Bethlehem. We can infer from the fact that the inspired writer does not mention any military work of his that the time of his judging was a peaceful time in which the people enjoyed calm, and his work was limited to judging his people and guiding them to God's commandments and law.

12.7.0.en: He had a large number of sons and daughters (thirty sons and thirty daughters), for the custom in that time was marrying more than one wife. And he gave his daughters in marriage to men from outside his clan or outside his city, perhaps because the clan was small, or there were no young men in the city suitable for becoming his in-laws. The period of his judging was seven years.

12.8.0.en: He died in quietness after begetting many sons and daughters and marrying them all off.

12.9.0.en: Ibzan was followed in judging by another judge, Elon the Zebulonite, called the Zebulonite because he was of the tribe of Zebulun. The inspired writer does not mention any wars that took place in his days, so he judged Israel in quietness ten years.

12.10.0.en: Elon: a town, the meaning of whose name is an oak, and perhaps oak trees were plentiful in this city, which lies in the portion of the tribe of Zebulun; it is different from the Elon that lies in the portion of the tribe of Dan (Josh 19:43). Elon died and was buried in his city, "the town of Elon," in the land of Zebulun.

12.11.0.en: Pirathon: it lies southwest of Nablus (Shechem) at a distance of 11 km.

12.11.1.en: After "Elon," "Abdon the son of Hillel" of the town of Pirathon in the land of Ephraim judged Israel.

12.12.0.en: It appears from the inspired text that he lived long, for he begat forty sons, and lived to see thirty grandsons, who also grew up to ride with their fathers on seventy ass colts, as was the way of the notables of the people in those times. The length of his judging was eight years.

12.13.0.en: He died and was buried in his town Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, beside the mountain named after the Amalekites, where the Amalekite people dwelt at one period of ancient history.

12.13.1.en: If God gives you peace, make use of it to live by His commandments and teach them to those around you, so that you bind everyone's hearts to Him and they are not disturbed if troubles come upon them because of their holding fast to God.

12.13.2.en: The birth of Samson (1) The angel of the LORD appears to Samson's mother (vv. 1-5:) 1 And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. 2 And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not. 3 And the angel of the LORD appeared unto the woman, and said unto her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son. 4 Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing: 5 For, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.

13.0.0.en: The Philistines: a strong people who dwelt in the south of the land of Canaan; they are of the descendants of the Caphtorim, who dwelt on the island of Crete and then migrated to these lands and took possession of them.

13.0.1.en: Beginning with this chapter and through the following three chapters, the inspired writer acquaints us with one of the most prominent judges of Israel and gives us many details about his life and works. In the first verse of this chapter he gives us the condition of the people of God before the birth of Samson. The people had suffered from the Philistines' enslaving them for forty years, which ended with what is related in (1 Sam 7:13), that is, in the days of Eli the priest. This was a divine punishment for them for turning away - again - from the worship of the living God, as though they had not benefited from the lessons of their former falls.

13.1.0.en: Zorah: a city at the southern edge of the tribe of Judah, about 14 miles west of Jerusalem and 23 miles southeast of Joppa (map 10). Here the inspired writer begins by mentioning Samson's family and the story of the good tidings of his birth. His father, whose name was "Manoah," was from the town of Zorah, of the tribe of the Danites. And Manoah's wife was barren.

13.2.0.en: The angel of the LORD: either an ordinary angel or one of the appearances of God, as proved by what is said in (vv. 17, 22) that his name is wonderful, and also by Manoah's saying "We have seen God" (v. 22). The angel of the LORD appeared to Manoah's wife, announcing to her that God would remove her barrenness and she would conceive and bear a son.

13.3.0.en: "Drink not wine nor strong drink": wine is fermented grape juice, with a small proportion of alcohol, while strong drink is aged wine with a large proportion of alcohol. This applies to any kind of wine, whether taken from grapes or from something else.

13.3.1.en: The angel commanded her not to drink wine or strong drink, and also warned her against eating what the law had forbidden of animals and birds (Lev 11). By this he meant her purity and her keeping away from forbidden strong drink, and also not being occupied with material pleasures, that is, drinking naturally fermented wine, which has a small proportion of alcohol.

13.3.2.en: This shows the importance of the preparation of expectant mothers to receive the newborn. Since they are a grace from God, they ought to prepare by strengthening their relationship with the Church and the Holy Sacraments, prayers and readings, and keeping away from sins in a repentance that purifies their souls, so that they may be worthy to be mothers of these children, and not affect their unborn children with any foreign substances that they drink.

13.4.0.en: "He shall begin to deliver": Samson began delivering his people from the Philistines, and Samuel, Saul and David completed the deliverance.

13.4.1.en: "No razor shall come on his head": hair was shaved with the razor, and the law of the Nazarite required that the Nazarite not shave his head throughout the period of his vow.

13.4.2.en: The purity which the angel required her to keep was necessary for her sanctification, because the son who would be born of her would be a Nazarite to the Lord from his birth and all his life, and had to apply the law of the Nazarite, as it is said in (Num 6:

13.4.3.en: 3-21), among which is that he not shave the hair of his head. The angel also announced to her that this son of hers would deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines.

13.4.4.en: (2) The angel instructs Manoah (vv. 6-14:) 6 Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of God came unto me, and his countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible: but I asked him not whence he was, neither told he me his name: 7 But he said unto me, Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink, neither eat any unclean thing: for the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death. 8 Then Manoah intreated the LORD, and said, O my Lord, let the man of God which thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born. 9 And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her. 10 And the woman made haste, and ran, and shewed her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the other day. 11 And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? And he said, I am. 12 And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass. How shall we order the child, and how shall we do unto him? 13 And the angel of the LORD said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware. 14 She may not eat of any thing that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing: all that I commanded her let her observe.

13.5.0.en: Manoah's wife was outside her house when the angel came to her, and when he spoke to her what is said in (vv. 4, 5) she hastened to the house to tell her husband what had happened, that a messenger from God had come to her whose appearance was awesome, and because of the awe of the situation she was not able to ask him where he had come from, and he too did not tell her his name.

13.6.0.en: She also told him the good tidings he had brought, that she would conceive and bear a son, and that she must not drink wine or anything intoxicating and must not eat any of the unclean foods that the law had forbidden, because her coming son would be a Nazarite to the Lord from his formation as an embryo in his mother's womb and throughout all the days of his life.

13.7.0.en: Manoah believed what his wife said, and since he was a devout man he prayed to God, asking that the angel whom He had sent to them return and make known to him how to deal with his son and guide him to the kind of upbringing in which he should raise him.

13.8.1.en: God answered Manoah's request, and the angel came again to his wife while she was in the field alone and her husband was not with her. It appears that Manoah's wife was devout, so he appeared to her first, and then a second time, while she was alone, before she called her husband.

13.9.0.en: The woman ran to where her husband was and told him that the messenger who had come to her some days before had appeared to her again in the field.

13.10.0.en: They hastened together to the field where his wife had seen the messenger, and he found him and asked him whether he was the very person who had spoken with his wife, and he answered him that he was the same.

13.11.0.en: Manoah said to him, when what he had announced to them was fulfilled, that God would give them a son, how they should act toward him in terms of upbringing and dealing with him, and what their duties toward him were.

13.11.1.en: It is good for parents to ask guidance and wisdom from the Lord in raising their children and dealing with them, so that they grow up in the fear of the Lord and grow in the bosom of the teachings of their mother Church, and thereby guard them from any deviations or evil company that might lead them into crooked ways; rather the word of the Lord embraces them and is their guide and educator, and the Lord blesses them and they grow spiritually, mentally and physically, and His blessing works in them and supports their steps.

13.12.0.en: "Anything that cometh of the vine": everything that comes from the grapevine, that is, moist grapes or raisins whose fermentation has begun.

13.12.1.en: The angel assured him that what was required of them was the same as he had said before to his wife at his first appearing to her, and repeated to him what he had commanded her, namely that she not eat of the grapes, which is the same as what is said in (Num 6:4) of details forbidding the Nazarite to eat anything fermented that comes from the grapevine; and that she not drink wine or any strong drink, and not eat of the birds and animals that the law had specified as unclean. He also repeated to him his warning to his wife that she keep entirely from all that he had mentioned to her. And Manoah and his wife carry out these warnings, and also the child who will be born to them and be a Nazarite to God.

13.12.2.en: (3) Manoah's feast for the angel (vv. 15-20:) 15 And Manoah said unto the angel of the LORD, I pray thee, let us detain thee, until we shall have made ready a kid for thee. 16 And the angel of the LORD said unto Manoah, Though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread: and if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the LORD. For Manoah knew not that he was an angel of the LORD. 17 And Manoah said unto the angel of the LORD, What is thy name, that when thy sayings come to pass we may do thee honour? 18 And the angel of the LORD said unto him, Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret? 19 So Manoah took a kid with a meat offering, and offered it upon a rock unto the LORD: and the angel did wondrously; and Manoah and his wife looked on. 20 For it came to pass, when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife looked on it, and fell on their faces to the ground.

13.13.0.en: "Let us detain thee": allow us to delay you for some time.

13.13.1.en: Manoah and his wife rejoiced at the good tidings, and desiring to honor the guest, and having thought the angel to be a man, a messenger or a prophet, they asked him to stay a little with them so that they might prepare something for him to eat, that is, slaughter a kid and cook it to perform the duty of hospitality toward him.

13.14.0.en: The angel answered him that even if he stayed with him a longer time and he offered him food, he would not eat of his food, and by this he drew Manoah's attention that he was not a man who eats and drinks. And the angel guided him that what he wished to offer, he should offer as a burnt offering to the Lord.

13.15.0.en: Up to this moment Manoah had not realized the identity of the man who was speaking to him, for he still believed that he was a man, that is, a prophet or a man of God, but in the end a man. Therefore he asked him his name, so that when what he had announced to them was fulfilled he might do for him what would express in a fitting way his thanks and gratitude to him.

13.16.0.en: The angel rejects Manoah's asking him his name, showing him that his name is wonderful, higher than his understanding. And God told Isaiah that His name shall be called Wonderful, referring to it (... Isa 9:6). He means that he is not a man but an angel from God, who has no ordinary name like the rest of mankind, or he is God Himself, whose name is above the names of all men.

13.17.0.en: Manoah obeyed the angel in what he guided him to, offering up the offering as a burnt offering to the Lord, so he took the kid and put it on a rock, which was like an altar, and kindled the fire in it, or put it there, and fire came out of the rock to consume the sacrifice, as happened with Gideon (ch. 6); and a wonderful thing accompanied that offering, at which Manoah and his wife were astonished, and the surprise stunned them, for they found the person who had been speaking to them ascending in the flame of the fire toward heaven, so they were greatly afraid and trembled at this wonderful sight, and bowed to the ground in awe and worship and thanksgiving to the God who had accepted their offering, because they were sure that this person was the angel of God or God Himself, for he is spirit and not a man with a body.

13.17.1.en: It is good to honor everyone who brings you glad tidings, and especially one who speaks to you about God and the salvation of your soul, for you honor God by honoring His servants, and He also, seeing your love, will bless you and reveal Himself to you more clearly.

13.17.2.en: (4) The birth of Samson (vv. 21-25:) 21 But the angel of the LORD did no more appear to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the LORD. 22 And Manoah said unto his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God. 23 But his wife said unto him, If the LORD were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things, nor would as at this time have told us such things as these. 24 And the woman bare a son, and called his name Samson: and the child grew, and the LORD blessed him. 25 And the Spirit of the LORD began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.

13.18.0.en: The coming out of the fire from the rock and the ascent of the angel in the flame of the fire confirmed to Manoah and his wife that the person who had spoken to them was the angel of the Lord, who had appeared to them in the form of a man. And with God's message having reached them, the angel ended his mission, and there was no need for him to appear to them again.

13.19.0.en: The children of Israel kept what Moses had said to them on the basis of the Lord's declaration to him that man shall not see God and live. And Manoah believed that the One who had appeared to him was God, who had appeared to him in some form, so he said to his wife that they would die immediately because they had seen God.

13.20.0.en: His wife was devout, so she reassured him, saying that if God had wanted them to die He would not have shown them those wonderful, joyful things: His glad tidings to them by means of the angel whom He sent to them, of their soon begetting a son who would be a Nazarite to the Lord, and also His acceptance of the offering from their hands by the coming out of the fire from the rock, which consumed the offering.

13.21.0.en: Samson: a word meaning exalted or great, or meaning the sun for its strength and greatness. The Lord's promise was fulfilled and Manoah's wife bore a son, after she had been barren, and called him Samson. And the boy grew spiritually and physically, and the Lord blessed him to qualify him for the great work that He would entrust to him.

13.22.0.en: Zorah: a city lying about 22 km west of Jerusalem on the border between the tribes of Dan and Judah.

13.22.1.en: Eshtaol: it lies about 2.5 km east of Zorah (map 10). The Spirit of the Lord began to work in him, and the features of a distinguished personality worthy of the esteem of his people appeared in him, and he was active among them in the region where the tribe of Dan dwelt, between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol.

13.22.2.en: The Spirit of God who worked in Samson dwells in you permanently and is able to bring you nearer to the worship of God and the love of all, if you submit to Him by repentance, holding fast to the commandments and accepting God's arrangements in your life.
